newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao charged in forgery case as woes mount.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao charged in forgery case as woes mount.

text.p: Indian federal police filed criminal charges on Thursday against former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, adding to the political leader's mounting legal troubles, authorities said.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said it filed charges against Rao and three others in connection with a case in 1989 in which documents were said to have been forged to tarnish the reputation of V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.
The criminal charges were believed to be the first against Rao, who is under investigation in at least two other cases but had not been indicted.
The CBI announced it had filed the charges only hours after a court rejected Rao's request for legal protection against arrest in another criminal case.

The twin legal blows came five days after Rao quit as head of the Congress party. He stepped down in disgrace on Saturday after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court next Monday as a co-accused in a criminal conspiracy case.
The forgery case involves the falsification of bank documents to show that V.P. Singh's son, Ajeya Singh, had a secret bank account with large amounts of money in the Caribbean island of St Kitts.

At the time V.P. Singh, who had left the ruling Congress party for the opposition, was spearheading an anti-corruption campaign against the government. V.P. Singh was appointed prime minister at the end of 1989 after Congress lost general elections.
Authorities later cleared Ajeya Singh of allegations that he had violated foreign exchange and anti-corruption laws.

The federal police agency said the Rao and the other three accused were charged with criminal conspiracy, forgery, giving false evidence and using forged documents. It did not say what possible penalties the charges carried.
Rao could not be reached for comment. A Congress spokesman said the party might comment on the charges later on Thursday.
The St Kitts case, which the CBI said would be taken up by a Delhi court next Tuesday, is one of several in which Rao has been named.

Earlier on Thursday, the Delhi High Court denied Rao's request for anticipatory bail in a $100,000 case of alleged conspiracy to cheat, court officials said. Anticipatory bail protects an accused against arrest.
Rao's lawyer had asked on Wednesday for anticipatory bail before a hearing next Monday in the cheating case.
Rao abruptly resigned as president of the Congress party on Saturday after a judge ordered him to appear in court as a co-accused at Monday's hearing.
Rao still remains head of Congress's parliamentary party, which includes all Congress MP's.
Indian expatriate businessman Lakhubhai Pathak alleges that Rao and a Hindu guru conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983.

Pathak says he paid the money to guru Chandraswami in an unsuccessful attempt to win a state newsprint contract after Rao, then foreign minister, assured Pathak at a meeting in a New York hotel that his "work would be done".
Rao has said he is innocent and has denied he was in New York on the dates mentioned by Pathak.
Chandraswami and an aide are being held in judicial custody in connection with the cheating case.
They were among the four charged in the St Kitts case on Thursday, the CBI said.
